dyson-star.title: A star as the source
dyson-star.text: We begin with the Sun. Light leaves the star in every direction. Power and flux are different quantities: power counts all the energy leaving each second; flux counts how much reaches each square metre at a particular distance. Our example uses the nominal solar luminosity. At one astronomical unit, the flux is about thirteen hundred and sixty-one watts per square metre. Double the distance and the flux falls to one quarter. The star still emits the same power. Bodies in this model are enlarged so you can see them. Orbital motion compresses years, and light markers illustrate paths: their physical travel speed is not solved. We are not counting any built coverage yet. Change the radius and check the figures before moving to the collector.

dyson-panel.title: Inside a collector
dyson-panel.text: Now we enter a one-square-metre reference plate. It is neither a real product nor a satellite we have just built. The Sun-facing surface absorbs light. Some becomes electricity, while the rest produces heat directly. Follow the connection to the load: we assume all electricity is used here, without storing it or sending it outside. Eventually it also becomes heat. That means electricity and final heat cannot be added as two independent gains: we would count the same energy twice. The editable efficiency changes the intermediate split. This isolated example plate emits thermal radiation from both faces. Its front surface, connections and radiators are separated to explain their functions. Sizes and marker speeds are illustrative; they do not describe a commercial machine.

dyson-swarm.title: Building coverage
dyson-swarm.text: We return to the system and add collectors on independent orbits. This chapter begins with zero coverage and reaches your chosen target. Each new portion of the swarm intercepts more light. In the ideal budget, eighteen percent coverage intercepts eighteen percent of solar power, while the remainder escapes. Coverage is an effective fraction you choose, not an estimate calculated from the area of these drawn plates. The figures are enlarged samples of a hypothetical population, not an inventory of real satellites. Circular orbits are calculated using solar gravity: more distant orbits have longer periods. We do not solve maneuvers, collisions, mutual shadows or component manufacturing. Growth in this chapter presents coverage; it is neither a construction schedule nor a prediction of exponential growth.

dyson-heat.title: Where the energy ends up
dyson-heat.text: Now watch the thermal output. Under our assumptions of local use and steady state, all intercepted power is eventually radiated: some becomes heat directly, and some first performs useful work. Orange markers show infrared in false color. A plate at about three hundred and thirty-one kelvin does not look red hot. That figure describes an isolated black plate at one astronomical unit, with two faces radiating freely. It is not a calculated temperature for a dense swarm: other collectors could block or return radiation. The graph compares reference blackbody spectra. A colder emitter peaks at longer wavelengths. An infrared excess would be a clue to investigate, not proof of technology: dust and other natural processes can also produce it. Change the radius or emissivity and follow the shifting peak.

dyson-mass.title: Radius, area and material
dyson-mass.text: Distance also changes the required area. Keep the same effective coverage and double the radius: the ideal area grows fourfold. With the same mass per square metre, total mass also increases by four. Surface density is an editable assumption, not a measured property of an available collector. This calculation counts only the ideal collecting surface. It excludes supports, manufacturing, payloads, transport, maintenance and shadows. The other side shows a separate historical comparison: spreading Jupiter's entire mass over a sphere at the selected radius. The resulting column and thickness illustrate a scale of material. They do not require dismantling Jupiter, and we are not simulating that process. Check how radius, flux, reference temperature, area and mass relate before visiting the shell.

dyson-shell.title: The shell comparison
dyson-shell.text: The final exhibit is a separate experiment with an idealized closed shell. It does not change the coverage target you saved for the swarm. The shell intercepts all the light, and only its outer surface can discharge energy to space. Assuming uniform temperature, the black-surface reference at one astronomical unit is about three hundred and ninety-four kelvin, above the isolated two-sided plate. We do not calculate the temperature of a partly built shell. Also watch the displaced star inside the uniform sphere. The shell theorem gives zero net gravitational force in its interior: there is no force to recenter it. This is not an animation of collapse or an automatically growing displacement. Structure, perturbations and active control raise other problems that we do not solve. Dyson's idea allows separate objects orbiting the star, without turning this rigid comparison into a buildable plan.
